# dsh-keyboard-shortcut

A Keyboard Shortcuts settings page for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), with permission-mode
cycling, reasoni

中文文档
## Overview

`dsh-keyboard-shortcut` adds one page to DSH's Settings panel and eight shortcuts
to the application

. The page lists every binding in the running application,
lets you change the ones this plugin owns

, and carries a switch for remapping the
composer's Enter keys.

Every shortcut this plugin adds is an ordinary DSH command. It appears in the
shortcut reference, it

can be rebound, and it respects the same conflict rules as
the built-in commands.
## Requirements
| Requirement | Minimum |

| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.0-rc.2` |
| Node.js (for building from source) | `22.12.0` |

This plugin is a **client plugin**: everything it does happens in the browser
half. Its Host half is

an empty `apply` that exists only so DSH serves the
browser bundle.

## What you get
### A Keyboard Shortcuts settings page

**Settings → Keyboard shortcuts** sits directly after General. It has four
sections:

- **Plugin shortcuts** — the commands this plugin owns, each row editable. Click
a row, press a comb

ination, and it saves. Press Escape to cancel.
- **Input navigation** — the two page-key shortcuts.

These have no command id,
so they are listed read-only rather than being rebindable; the reason is u

nder
Known limitations.
- **Input optimisation** — the composer key switch described below.
- **Appl

ication shortcuts** — every other registered command, read-only. This is
the table that makes a bind

ing conflict comprehensible: when a combination is
refused, the row that already owns it is visible

comprehensible: when a combination is
refused, the row that already owns it is visible right there.
### Shortcuts
| Shortcut | Action | Platforms |

| Ctrl+Q | Cycle to the next permission mode | Desktop Windows, macOS |
| Ctrl+1 | Lower the reasoni

ng effort one level | Desktop |
| Ctrl+2 | Raise the reasoning effort one level | Desktop |
| Alt+A

| Open the DeepSeek status page in the sidebar browser | Desktop |
| Ctrl+L | Expand or collapse the

task list | Desktop |
| PgUp | Go to the previous input | All (fixed) |
| PgDn | Go to the next inp

ut | All (fixed) |
| Ctrl+/ | Open this plugin's settings page | All |

Ctrl/Cmd+/ is the built-in shortcut reference's
default binding. This plugin claims it through the s

hortcut preference layer, so
the reference dialog moves off that key and stays reachable from **Sett

ings →
General → Edit shortcuts**. Turning the switch off restores the original
binding.
### Input optimisation
When enabled, the composer's three Enter gestures rotate:
| Stroke | Default | With input optimisation |

| Enter | Send | Insert a line break |
| Ctrl+Enter | Complementary Queue/Steer | Send |
| Shift+Ent
er | Insert a line break | Complementary Queue/Steer |
The switch is off by default.

## Known limitations

- **Cycle, effort, status-page and task-list shortcuts are Desktop-only by
default.** DSH reserves C

trl+Q outside Desktop Windows
and macOS, and browsers claim Ctrl+1…Ctrl+8
for tab switching. Alt+A a

nd Ctrl+L
are not admitted by the browser allowlist at all — a single non-primary
modifier is refuse

d, and both keys are spoken for. All five commands exist on
every platform and can be bound by hand;

they simply ship unbound where the
combination cannot work.
- **The DSH Desktop shell is classified

as a browser by the shortcut service.**
It publishes no `html[data-platform]` marker — that marker

would make the
service demand a native keyboard bridge the shell does not provide, and the
service t

hrows without one — so `desktop:*` defaults never resolve and the
registry refuses to store the comb

inations above. The plugin detects the
window itself and delivers them through `observeFixedInput`,

the same raw-input
path the page keys use. A registry binding always wins, so one press never runs
a

n action twice, and a combination a desktop window also reserves
(Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, …) is never taken

over. See docs/shortcuts.md.
- **The status-page shortcut reuses a page, not a tab.** The sidebar br

owser
registers itself as a tab type that may appear more than once, so opening it
through the sideb

ar's own API always mints a new tab. The plugin therefore
looks for a browser tab that is *showing t

he status page* and reveals it,
expanding the column if it is collapsed. A tab on another address is

left alone
and the status page opens beside it, and a tab belonging to another session is
ignored,

because the sidebar only reveals tabs in the session on screen.
- **The task-list toggle clicks the

panel header.** DSH keeps the collapsed
state inside the panel component and exposes no handle, so t

he shortcut drives
the same button a click would. A session with no task list shows nothing to
toggl

e, which the shortcut reports instead of failing.
- **Prompt navigation drives the turn rail.** DSH

publishes no service for
jumping to a turn, so the shortcut activates the rail's own marks. A turn i
